short_title: Seagrass as a record of metal pollution over time (2017)
title: Biomonitoring of coastal pollution in the Gulf of Gabes (SE, Tunisia): use of Posidonia oceanica seagrass as a bioindicator and its mat as an archive of coastal metallic contamination
summary: Measured cadmium, copper, lead and zinc in seagrass tissue and in the layers of the seagrass mat. Deeper (older) layers had lower metal levels, which the authors read as pollution rising over recent decades. Seagrass meadows have shrunk or disappeared in parts of the central Gulf.

findings.headline: Seagrass layers suggest pollution has risen for decades
findings.summary: Metal levels fell from shallow (recent) to deep (older) layers of the seagrass mat, which the authors interpret as continuously increasing pollution over recent decades.
